scope.summary: Closed residual F10/F11 mounted-frontend failures and established the mandatory full-application TypeScript gate (Q01) after the FE-STRICTLIVE-001 and FE-EXACT-PAIR-PROTOCOL-001 predecessors. F10: src/management/pages/v5/V5Pages.tsx was missing the Badge import used in 3 places on the mounted V5 loops page. F11: src/management/components/agent/AgentPanelBody.tsx's Codex reauth flow referenced an undefined setControlTargetMode (dead vestigial call with no backing state) and an undefined agentPanel (the real singleton exists in useAgentPanel.ts but was never imported) in its focusPanel("agentPanel") branch; both now use real in-scope state and the real panel API, preserving the intended reauth/focus semantics rather than deleting the branches. Q01: rebaselined the frozen 397-diagnostic audit against current dev after predecessor merges; found 434 diagnostics across ~70 files (audit drift is explicitly anticipated by this task's own acceptance criteria). Fixed all of them: the largest single root cause (~150 diagnostics) was the generated WorkshopCard DTO typing `payload` as `Record<string, never>` and omitting several real server-emitted card_type values already handled by WorkshopCardRenderer -- fixed by giving workshops.ts (the consumer/adapter boundary) its own WorkshopCard type instead of aliasing the incomplete generated shape, per this task's explicit instruction not to hand-edit generated types.ts. A second systemic root cause: tsconfig.app.json has strict:false (strictNullChecks off), which breaks TypeScript's discriminated-union narrowing for boolean-literal discriminants on `if (!result.ok)` / `if (result.ok) {} else {}` patterns used throughout the BFF result-union call sites -- fixed at each call site by switching to explicit `=== false` / `=== true` (or string-literal `kind`) comparisons, which narrow correctly regardless of strictNullChecks; tsconfig itself was left untouched. Remaining diagnostics were genuine, independent type-contract misalignments (renamed/missing DTO fields, stale test fixtures using pre-refactor field names, wrong literal unions, unnarrowed `unknown` values) fixed at the real consumer/adapter boundary in each audited file. Four additional files (src/lib/bff-v1/evolution.ts, src/management/pages/ResearchDetail.tsx, src/management/pages/ResearchDetail.test.tsx, src/test/hosted-browser-release-policy.test.ts) were formally added to the task artifact contract by Human/Ops at 2026-09-17T00:21:08Z; all 13 residual diagnostics across these files were cleanly closed without touching central/generated types. Added package.json `typecheck:app` (full app) / `typecheck:agora` (existing focused Agora gate, kept as the acceptance criteria instruct) and repointed `typecheck` at the full-app gate; branch-ci.yml's required Typecheck step now runs both. Added src/test/full-app-typecheck-contract.test.ts to lock this gate in place against regression.

lazyNamedRoute's generic constraint required the entire imported route module to satisfy Record<string, RouteComponent>, which broke when a route module also exports a plain non-component helper (safeWorkshopReturnPath in routes/agora.tsx). Narrowed the constraint to only require the named export key to be a RouteComponent (Record<Key, RouteComponent>) instead of the whole module shape.

New contract test (declared artifact) that locks the Q01 CI gate in place: asserts tsconfig.app.json's include root is "src" (the real app root), npm run typecheck / typecheck:app resolve to tsc -p tsconfig.app.json, typecheck:agora remains available, and required branch CI actually runs both npm run typecheck:app and npm run typecheck:agora -- so the full-app gate cannot silently regress back to the narrower Agora-only check.

Rebaseline fix: `new Promise((r) => s.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", r))` resolved to the wrong Node http.Server#listen overload (TS picked the (port, backlog, callback) signature). Wrapped the callback explicitly and typed the executor as Promise<void>.
